name: Alice Guy Blaché
quote: There is nothing connected with the making of a film that a woman cannot do as easily as a man, being fully capable of mastering every technical detail of this art.

profile.content: Alice was born in Saint-Mandé in 1873. At age 6, Alice was sent to France to study at the Convent of the Sacred Heart, on the border with Switzerland, along with her siblings. After her father's death, Alice trained as a stenographer and typist, new fields at the time, in order to support her mother and herself. She got her first job at a varnish factory. A year later, in 1894, she began working with Léon Gaumont at the Comptoir général de la photographie.

In 1894, Alice was hired by Gaumont to work at the photography company as a secretary. The company soon collapsed, but Gaumont bought its inventory and started his own company, which would soon become a pioneering powerhouse of the French film industry. Alice decided to stay with Gaumont at his new company, the "Gaumont Film Company", a decision that would lead her to become a pioneer. On March 22, 1895, Alice and Gaumont attended the Lumières' surprise screening, where they showed one of the first films ever made, La Sortie de l'usine Lumière à Lyon.

In mid-1896, Alice released the world's first production with a cinematic narrative, La Fée aux choux (The Cabbage Fairy). From 1896 to 1906, she was head of production at Gaumont's studio and probably the only woman film director of that period. In 1906, she shot The Life of Christ, a large-scale production for its time, with three hundred extras.

In 1907, Alice married Herbert Blaché, who was soon put in charge of production for Gaumont's operations in the United States. After working with her husband in the United States, the two decided to set up their own company in 1910 with George A. Magie, thus creating the Solax Company, the largest film studio before Hollywood, with Alice being the first woman, or one of the first, to run a studio.

To focus solely on writing and directing, she handed the presidency of Solax over to Herbert. The couple tried to keep up a partnership for a while, but the relationship was short-lived. Herbert left his wife and children to try for a career in Hollywood with another actress.

Alice directed her last film in 1920, nearly dying of the flu during the production. On March 24, 1968, Alice died at the age of ninety-four while living in a nursing home.

name: Martin Scorsese
quote: Desde que me lembro, sempre quis ser um gangster. Para mim, ser gangster era melhor que ser presidente dos Estados Unidos.

profile.content: Martin Scorsese was born in New York. He graduated from NYU's film school, drawing attention with short films such as It's Not Just You, Murray! (1964). He directed his first feature, I Call First (1967), was assistant director and co-editor of Woodstock (1970), and directed Boxcar Bertha (1972) for producer Roger Corman.

Launching one of the most acclaimed director-actor partnerships, Scorsese and Robert De Niro made Mean Streets, the first in a series of eight films. In 1980 came Raging Bull, a biography of boxer Jake La Motta, featuring lush black-and-white cinematography and a true tour de force performance by De Niro. Scorsese also made New York, New York (1977), a musical starring Liza Minnelli and De Niro, and The Last Waltz (1978), a film about the farewell concert of the group The Band.

The rest of the decade proved less receptive to Scorsese's originality. Although appreciated today, The King of Comedy (1982) was a failure. The Last Temptation of Christ (1988) received good reviews but was mired in controversy, sparking vehement protests from religious groups and being banned in some countries.

A reunion with De Niro produced the perfect mob film, Goodfellas (1990), a sinister remake of Cape Fear (1991), and Casino (1995). In 1990, the director created The Film Foundation, dedicated to film preservation. He directed the beautiful Kundun in 1997, a biography of the Dalai Lama.

Gangs of New York (2002) marked the beginning of a new collaboration with Leonardo DiCaprio, which would include The Aviator (2004) and The Departed (2006), the latter earning Scorsese a long-overdue Oscar. The Grammy-winning No Direction Home (2005) and Shine a Light (2008) continued his long involvement with the music documentary, celebrating the work of Bob Dylan and the Rolling Stones, respectively.

awards: 6 wins, including 2 OFTA Film Hall of Fame and 1 honorary Oscar.

name: Georges Méliès
quote: He greets his audience as the dreamers and adventurers they truly are and invites them to dream along with him.

profile.content: Georges Méliès was born in 1861. He gained fame in Paris as an illusionist, founding the Théâtre Robert-Houdin.

Méliès began making films in the style of the Lumière brothers, but then discovered the camera's potential for illusion, essentially inventing special effects. His early films, just one reel long, were simple demonstrations of magic tricks such as transformations and disappearances.
He went on to make more complex films with multiple special-effects sequences linked by more elaborate plots. His last epics were seldom seen.
Bankrupt and out of filmmaking, Méliès was hailed as a master by the Surrealists and won national recognition: in 1931 he received the Legion of Honor.

name: Sergei Eisenstein
quote: The profession of film director can and should be so lofty and precious that no one may aspire to it while turning away from any knowledge that would make him a better director of films or a better human being.

profile.content: After a brief stint in the army, Sergei Eisenstein joined the theater in 1920. His first feature film was Strike (1925), followed the same year by Battleship Potemkin.

International recognition was key to Eisenstein obtaining permission to make October (1928), commemorating the 10th anniversary of the October Revolution. Charlie Chaplin (1889-1977) introduced him to the American writer Upton Sinclair, and together they began a project in Mexico that was never completed.

Eisenstein spent a period teaching and left a film, Bezhin Meadow (1937), unfinished, which led Stalin to view him with disfavor. After receiving a pardon, he returned with Alexander Nevsky (1938, see p. 142), a warning about the Nazi threat.

Ivan the Terrible, Part I (1944) was regarded as a portrait of the strength of the Russian people and their indomitable leader. In 1946, the director finished shooting the second part of this epic, but its depiction of leadership degenerating into tyranny enraged Stalin, and it was released only in 1958. Eisenstein suffered a heart attack while working on the third and final part of the film and died on February 11, 1948. The trilogy was never completed.

name: Buster Keaton
quote: A comedian does strange things. A good comedian does funny things.

profile.content: Joseph Frank Keaton was born on October 4, 1895. His family performed in vaudeville, and he made his stage debut in 1899.

Keaton appeared in his first film, The Butcher Boy (1917), opposite Fatty Arbuckle. His screen persona was already established, including his signature porkpie hat. His first leading role was in The Saphead (1920). Joseph M. Schenck found the young star so promising that he gave him his own production company, Buster Keaton Comedies.

This period was Keaton's golden age, in which his stone-faced character, daring sequences, and occasionally melancholic tone elevated his work above the studio comedies. Our Hospitality (1923) was followed by Sherlock Jr. and The Navigator (both 1924), College (1927), Steamboat Bill, Jr. and The Cameraman (both 1928). In all of his films, Keaton's characters are desperate to escape chaos and find solace in a simpler life.

Executives at MGM, Keaton's new studio, tried to rein in any excessive spending after the failure of The General. Ironically, his bland pairings with Jimmy Durante, especially What! No Beer? (1933), the last feature film starring Keaton, were among his biggest box-office hits.

In addition to a few notable cameos, including a guest appearance as a card player in Sunset Boulevard (1950), Keaton played small comic roles in a number of films, among them Around the World in 80 Days (1956) and It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World (1963). At 68, he starred in Film (1965), a 24-minute picture written by Samuel Beckett.
His last screen appearance was alongside Zero Mostel in A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum, directed by Richard Lester (born 1932). Keaton died on February 1, 1966, in California.

awards: Won 1 Oscar. Another 147 wins and 221 nominations

name: Quentin Tarantino
quote: If you want to make a film, make it. Don't wait for funding, don't wait for perfect circumstances. Just make it.

profile.content: At 16, Quentin began studying acting at the James Best Theatre Company. At 22, he wrote his first screenplay, Captain Peachfuzz and the Anchovy Bandit. In 1984, Tarantino started working as a clerk at Video Archives.

He met Lawrence Bender at a party in Hollywood, who encouraged him to direct a film. The end result of that conversation was Reservoir Dogs. He turned down several projects, such as Speed and Men in Black, withdrew to Amsterdam, and began working on his screenplay for Pulp Fiction, which was released in 1994 and won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival.

After Pulp Fiction, he directed the fourth segment of the anthology Four Rooms, The Man from Hollywood, a remake of an episode of Alfred Hitchcock Presents starring Steve McQueen. In 1997, he released his third film, Jackie Brown, a tribute to the blaxploitation genre. In 2003, he released Kill Bill, issued in two parts, Vol. 1 and Vol. 2, a project he created together with the film's lead actress, Uma Thurman, during the shooting of Pulp Fiction.

In partnership with Robert Rodriguez, Tarantino wrote and directed Death Proof, in addition to making guest appearances on American TV series. In 2009, he released one of his most acclaimed works, Inglourious Basterds, starring Brad Pitt, Christoph Waltz, Mélanie Laurent, and Diane Kruger. Four years later, he released Django Unchained, renewing his partnership with Christoph Waltz.

The Hateful Eight was released in 2015, shot in 70 mm and, for the first time, featuring an original score composed by Ennio Morricone, something the Italian had not done for a western in more than 34 years. Following the rape allegations against Harvey Weinstein in 2017, Tarantino released his newest film, Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, through Sony Pictures.

awards: Won 2 Oscars. Another 140 wins and 183 nominations.

name: Christopher Nolan
quote: Mankind was born on Earth, but it will not die here.

profile.content: After working on several short films, such as Tarantella, Larceny, and Doodlebug, he gained notoriety and caught the attention of the studios. In 1998, he released his first feature film, Following, and two years later, Memento (2000), acclaimed by critics who praised its unique nonlinear structure and its various themes, such as memory, perception, and revenge. In 2002, he released Insomnia, starring Al Pacino, Robin Williams, and Hilary Swank.

In early 2003, Nolan approached Warner Bros. with the idea of making a new Batman film. The film was released in 2005, with Christian Bale in the title role, alongside Michael Caine and Gary Oldman. After releasing his film The Prestige, Nolan released the second film of the Batman trilogy, The Dark Knight. Released in 2008 to immense critical acclaim, The Dark Knight has been regarded as one of the best films of the 2000s and one of the best superhero films of all time. At the 81st Academy Awards, it was nominated in eight categories, winning for "Best Sound Editing" and, posthumously, "Best Supporting Actor" for Heath Ledger's performance as the Joker.

In 2010, Nolan wrote and directed Inception, another critical and commercial success, before releasing the final film of the Batman trilogy, known as the "Dark Knight" trilogy: The Dark Knight Rises. In 2014, Interstellar, starring Matthew McConaughey, Anne Hathaway, Jessica Chastain, and Michael Caine, was released, receiving five Oscar nominations.

Nolan went on to serve as a producer on other Warner superhero films, such as Man of Steel and Batman v Superman: Dawn of Justice. In 2017, he released Dunkirk, which received 5 Oscar nominations, one of them Nolan's first for Best Director.

awards: Nominated for 5 Oscars. Another 136 wins and 217 nominations.
